title: Introduction to Technology and Careers
description: This course exposes students to the field of mechatronics and control system disciplines. The course presents basic skills necessary to succeed as mechatronics student. The nature of control system in different process industries and the role of mechatronics technicians are explored. Communication skills for reports are developed. Guest speakers from local process firms and tours to local companies are included.
outcomes: Collect, organize, and present measurement data in tabular and graphic form.
Measuring DC voltage, DC current, and resistance
Comparison of DC and AC circuits
Identify both process variable and control variable in a manufacturing process
Identify and understanding different process industries, e.g. pharmaceutical, water and wastewater, electronic parts, and oil & refinery.
objectives: Overview of the field of mechatronics and control system career
Communication skills for reports are developed
Describe, compare, and contrast voltage, current, power, efficiency, energy, resistance, and various pneumatic system.
content: Difference between Engineering Technology and Engineering
Future technology career prospects in the Silicon Valley and beyond
History of Mechatronics and its impact on various industries
Analyzing and presenting data using MS Excel/Google Sheets
Expose students to idea of control systems: define Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)/Human Machine Interface (HMI)/Operator Interface Terminal (OIT)/Distributed Control System (DCS)
Working effectively within a team of technicians and engineering team
lab: Explore Tools Used by Mechatronics technicians: MS Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PLC program
assignments: Outside assignments are reading and homework assignments. Students prepare presentations outside of class.
For example: Deliver a presentation on the role of mechatronics in a process industry

Students will analyze and present solutions to engineering technology problems related to current technology issues. The students will also discuss the presentations of guest speakers and analyze how they relate to their own interests and experiences. Numerous applications of the engineering technology problem solving process will be presented throughout the semester.
For example: "Identify and analyze the automation issues with autonomous vehicles."

The students deliver weekly written homework assignments addressing topics such as why they chose to study mechatronics, how do they prepare for exams, what is their problem-solving process. In addition to the weekly assignments, the students deliver a report of their mechatronics field work.
A typical writing assignment may be the following: "How does automation impact your life?”

Another typical presentation assignment is to have students present about someone in STEM. As many of our students work day jobs in STEM companies, they can share their current job as assemblers or lower-level technicians. Others are asked to research and find people who have these roles.
